observations: A treadle (manual, foot-pedal) sewing machine mounted in a wooden cabinet/table.
Machine head has visible brand lettering reading 'MERCURY' (clearest in photo 1 and photo 2).
Body shows chipped paint, scratches, and surface rust spots on the metal housing (photo 1, photo 2).
Wooden table/cabinet is reddish-brown, with some wear on edges and a drawer on one side (photo 3).
Cast-iron treadle base and flywheel visible underneath, with a ventilated metal foot plate bearing a worn brand mark (photo 2, photo 3), text not legible.
No visible electric motor or power cord; mechanism appears to be purely foot-treadle operated.
Photos are all static, no video or clip showing the needle, foot pedal, or stitching in motion.
Background shows an outdoor setting (dirt yard, signage), consistent with a casual resale photo shoot.

identity.kind: treadle sewing machine with wooden cabinet

claims.evidence: Photo 1 and photo 2 show chipped paint, scratches, and rust spots on the machine head, which is inconsistent with 'perfect condition'.

risks.risk: Mechanical function unknown: whether the needle, bobbin, and treadle mechanism actually move smoothly and stitch properly.
risks.proof: A short video clip of the treadle being pedaled and the needle moving through fabric, stitching a sample line.

risks.risk: Rust or corrosion on internal moving parts (shaft, gears, bobbin case) not visible from exterior photos.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the underside mechanism and bobbin area with the faceplate removed.
risks.if_unproven: priced as having moderate mechanical wear/risk, not fully functional

risks.risk: Condition of the wooden cabinet (warping, water damage, woodworm) beyond what is visible in outdoor lighting.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the cabinet joints, underside, and drawer interior.
risks.if_unproven: priced as cosmetic-only wood, no premium for cabinet quality

risks.risk: Completeness of accessories (bobbins, needles, belt, manual) not shown.
risks.proof: Photo of accessory kit or belt condition close-up.

risks.risk: Belt condition (treadle drive belt) could be cracked or missing, affecting usability.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the belt connecting the wheel to the machine head.

proof_requests: Video of the treadle being pedaled with the needle stitching a piece of fabric.
Close-up photo of the belt and flywheel connection.
Close-up photo of the underside/bobbin mechanism.
Close-up photo of the cabinet's drawers and joints for wood condition.
Clear photo of any model/serial plate on the machine, if present.
response.reason: The item is clearly identifiable as a Mercury-branded treadle sewing machine in a wooden cabinet, but visible cosmetic wear contradicts the 'perfect condition' claim and no proof of working mechanism is given, so it must be priced at worst case (cosmetically worn, functionality unverified).
